newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NFI ZACHODNI SEEKS TO LIST FOUR FIRMS IN 97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NFI ZACHODNI SEEKS TO LIST FOUR FIRMS IN 97.

text.p: National Investment Fund (NFI) Zachodni (No 14) in Poland's mass privatisation programme plans to list four of its firms on the Warsaw bourse this year, the fund's deputy president said on Thursday.

"In June 1997 we plan to submit prospectuses to the Securities Commission for two firms, one of them (engineering firm) Ponar Wadowice, which is a candidate for the parallel market," Robert Oppenheim told Reuters.
He said the fund later this year planned to find strategic investors for another four of its firms.

Oppenheim said smaller firms in Zachodni's portfolio might have shares sold to management and that the fund also sought to invest in firms not traded publicly. He said cash that could be freely invested accounted for 25 percent of the fund's assets.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equity stakes in the remaining firms.
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been entitled to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
Oppenheim said his fund would generally not take dividends from firms in its portfolio and allow them to reinvest profits. He added it had only done so in one case concerning 1996 earnings.
He said the fund sought to up its stake in 50 firms in which it had a 1.9-percent stake, 15 of them this year.
